questions.text: The correct match between Item-I and Item-II is:
options: A → R ; B → S ; C → P ; D → Q
A → Q ; B → P ; C → S ; D → R
A → Q ; B → S ; C → P ; D → R
A → R ; B → P ; C → S ; D → Q
questions.sol_text:
We need to match drugs in Item-I with their corresponding identification tests in Item-II.

Item-I (Drugs):
(A) Chloroxylenol - an antiseptic phenol with OH group and Cl substituent
(B) Norethindrone - a steroid hormone with C=C double bond (unsaturation)
(C) Sulphapyridine - a sulfonamide with amino group
(D) Penicillin - a beta-lactam antibiotic

Item-II (Tests):
(P) Carbylamine test - detects primary amines (-NH2) by reaction with CHCl3 and KOH
(Q) Sodium hydrogen carbonate test - detects carboxylic acids (-COOH)
(R) Ferric chloride test - detects phenols (-OH groups)
(S) Bayer's test - detects unsaturation (C=C double bonds)

Matching:
A (Chloroxylenol) → R (Ferric chloride test) - because chloroxylenol has OH group (phenol)
B (Norethindrone) → S (Bayer's test) - because norethindrone has C=C unsaturation
C (Sulphapyridine) → P (Carbylamine test) - because sulphapyridine has primary amino group
D (Penicillin) → Q (Sodium hydrogen carbonate test) - because penicillin has carboxylic acid group (-COOH)

Therefore: A → R ; B → S ; C → P ; D → Q

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The antifertility drug "Novestrol" can react with
questions.sol_text:
Ethynylestradiol (novestrol) contains the following functional groups:

1. A phenolic OH group on the benzene ring
2. An alkyne (C ≡ CH) group in the side chain
3. Secondary alcohols in the steroid structure

Let us analyze each reaction:

(1) Br2/water ; ZnCl2/HCl ; FeCl3
- Br2/water: Reacts with the alkyne (C ≡ CH) and the phenolic OH group (addition and substitution)
- ZnCl2/HCl: Lucas test - reacts with alcohols to form alkyl chlorides
- FeCl3: Ferric chloride test - gives purple/violet color with phenolic OH group
This combination detects all three functional groups. ✓

(2) Alcoholic HCN ; NaOCl ; ZnCl2/HCl
- Alcoholic HCN: Reacts with carbonyl groups (not present in significant amounts)
- NaOCl: Oxidizes alcohols and phenols
- ZnCl2/HCl: Lucas test for alcohols
No detection of alkyne. ✗

(3) ZnCl2/HCl ; FeCl3 ; Alcoholic HCN
- ZnCl2/HCl: Lucas test for alcohols
- FeCl3: Test for phenols
- Alcoholic HCN: No reaction with the functional groups present
Does not detect alkyne effectively. ✗

(4) Br2/water ; ZnCl2/HCl ; NaOCl
- Br2/water: Reacts with alkyne and phenol
- ZnCl2/HCl: Lucas test for alcohols
- NaOCl: Oxidizing agent, not a specific functional group test
Lacks the specific phenolic test (FeCl3). ✗

The correct answer is [1] because it provides the three specific tests:
- Br2/water for alkyne and phenol reactivity
- ZnCl2/HCl for alcohol functional groups
- FeCl3 for phenolic OH confirmation

questions.sol_text: Brompheniramine is a first-generation antihistamine medication. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A chemist has 4 samples of artificial sweetener A, B, C and D. To identify these samples, he performed certain experiments and noted the following observations: (i) A and D both form blue-violet colour with ninhydrin. (ii) Lassaigne extract of C gives positive AgNO3 test and negative Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3 test. (iii) Lassaigne extract of B and D gives positive sodium nitroprusside test. Based on these observations which option is correct?
options: A : Aspartame; B : Alitame; C : Saccharin; D : Sucralose
A : Aspartame; B : Saccharin; C : Sucralose; D : Alitame
A : Alitame; B : Saccharin; C : Aspartame; D : Sucralose
A : Saccharin; B : Alitame; C : Sucralose; D : Aspartame
questions.sol_text:
A – Aspartame
B – Saccharin
C – Sucralose
D – Alitame

(i) A & D give positive test with ninhydrin because both have free carboxylic and amine group.
    Aspartame has both -COOH and -NH2 groups, so it gives positive ninhydrin test.
    Alitame also has both -COOH and -NH2 groups, so it gives positive ninhydrin test.

(ii) C form precipitate with AgNO3 because it has chlorine atoms.
     Sucralose contains chlorine atoms, so it gives positive AgNO3 test.
     The negative Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3 test indicates absence of Fe2+ ions, which rules out compounds containing iron.

(iii) B & D give positive test because Both have S-atom.
      Saccharin contains S-atom in its structure, so it gives positive sodium nitroprusside test.
      Alitame contains S-atom in its structure, so it gives positive sodium nitroprusside test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Two statements in respect of drug-enzyme interaction are given below. Statement I: Action of an enzyme can be blocked only when an inhibitor blocks the active site of the enzyme. Statement II: An inhibitor can form a strong covalent bond with the enzyme. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol_text: Statement I is false because enzyme action can be blocked not only by inhibitors blocking the active site, but also through various mechanisms like competitive inhibition, non-competitive inhibition, and irreversible inhibition. Statement II is true because inhibitors can form strong covalent bonds with enzymes (irreversible inhibitors), which destroy the catalytic activity of enzymes. Inhibitors interact with functional groups on the enzyme surface and can reduce or completely destroy catalytic activity.

questions.subject: Chemistry

(c) Competitive Drugs are allosteric site blocking drugs. (d) Non-competitive Drugs are active site blocking drugs. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.sol_text: Drugs can inhibit the attachment of substrate on active site of Enzyme in two ways: (1) Competitive, (2) Non-competitive. Competitive inhibitors bind on the active site of Enzymes. Non-Competitive inhibitors bind on allosteric site. Therefore, statements (a), (b) are correct. Statement (c) is incorrect because Competitive Drugs block active sites, not allosteric sites. Statement (d) is incorrect because Non-competitive Drugs block allosteric sites, not active sites.

Both statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.sol_text:
• Noradrenaline is a neurotransmitter.
• Low level of noradrenaline is a cause for depression in human.

Statement I is correct: Noradrenaline is indeed a neurotransmitter that plays an important role in the nervous system.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A : Antihistamines do not affect the section of acid in stomach. Reason R : Antiallergic and antacid drugs work on different receptors. In the light of the above statements, Choose the correct answer from the option given below.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false
questions.sol_text:
Antihistamines not affect the secretion of acid in stomach, the reason is that antiallergic and antacid drugs work on different receptors.

Assertion A is TRUE: Antihistamines do not affect the secretion of acid in the stomach because they work on H1 receptors (responsible for allergic reactions), not on H2 receptors (which regulate acid secretion).

Reason R is TRUE: Antiallergic drugs (antihistamines) work on H1 receptors while antacid drugs work on H2 receptors, which are different receptors.

Reason R is the CORRECT EXPLANATION of A: The reason why antihistamines do not affect acid secretion is precisely because antiallergic and antacid drugs work on different receptors.

Therefore, both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
